items.title: Create the Cargo workspace with the crate topology from the proposal.
Write `PRINCIPLES.md` at the repository root, containing the eight non-negotiables verbatim plus the operationalization table.
Adopt a Conventional-Commits-compatible commit policy with signed commits required on `main`.
Build the CI matrix: Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64, macOS x86_64, macOS aarch64, Windows x86_64.
Add `cargo-deny` (licence and advisory policy), `cargo-machete` (unused deps), and `cargo-clippy` with `-D warnings` to CI.
Establish the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process and template; create `docs/adr/`.
Add the PR template that requires naming any Principle the change touches.
Configure branch protection on `main`: required review, required CI, signed commits, linear history.
Set up the security policy, `SECURITY.md`, and a private vulnerability reporting channel.
Establish the release-engineering pipeline: versioning, changelog generation, artifact signing hooks.
Delete the scratch verification crate at `.scratch/witprobe` once its findings are folded into the test suite; port its three assertions into `crates/qqq-host/tests/`.
Install `wasm-tools` and the `wasmtime` CLI into the developer bootstrap script (both were found missing on the reference machine).

Keep the executive summary in the Proposal synchronised with reality: re-verify its three falsifiable claims against the benchmark suite and the security artifacts at every milestone, and correct them publicly when they no longer hold.
Create `README.md` — the public front door (see `QQQ-Observations-and-Memories.md §D-009` for the brief).
Create `QQQ-Proposal-V1.md` as the canonical technical proposal.
Create `QQQ-Checklist-V1.md` as the canonical work breakdown.
Create `QQQ-Observations-and-Memories.md` as the institutional-memory record.
Add a `docs/README.md` index that explains the three-document system and how to keep them in sync.
Build `tools/check-xrefs/` — the cross-reference validator described in the proposal.
Wire `check-xrefs` into CI as a required check.
Document the anchor derivation and stability rules in `docs/contributing/anchors.md`.
Implement the stub-marker convention (`// QQQ-STUB(<ID>): …`) and a CI check that every stub marker has a matching Observations entry.
Implement the tombstone convention for retired anchors and add a CI check that no anchor is silently deleted.
Publish `docs/glossary.md` generated from the Proposal glossary, with anchors.
Add a CI check that every glossary term used in WIT doc comments exists in the glossary.
Maintain `docs/reconciliation.md` tracking every correction made to the source corpus, kept in sync with Appendix A.
Publish the vocabulary and claims rules as `docs/contributing/claims-policy.md`.
Add the "framework vs runtime" usage rule to the contributing guide.
Publish `docs/verified-facts.md` as the live, dated register of external facts the project depends on, with a re-verification cadence.
Generate the WIT reference documentation from `wit/` into Markdown, with per-language examples.
Build the documentation freshness test: compile a sample project against the published docs and fail on drift.
Publish the error catalogue generator: every `QQQ-XXXX` code becomes a docs page with cause, fix and example.
Publish `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` at the repository root and on the docs site.
Draft `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0) for the runtime repository.
Obtain legal review of the Apache-2.0 grant and the irrevocability commitment for the V1 line.

Define the free-entity grant precisely: individuals, solo developers, non-profits, and companies under $2M revenue.

Configure `cargo-deny` to enforce the dependency licence allowlist.

Define the RFC process for changes to `PRINCIPLES.md` and to published anchors.

Write the four-shift narrative as a standalone, citable essay.

Establish the vocabulary-discipline lint: forbidden phrases in docs and blog posts.
Define the "agent sandbox" positioning as the beachhead and validate it with design partners.
Resolve the TypeScript-versus-AssemblyScript naming question (open question `OQ-002`).
Write the layered-architecture ADR fixing the nine layers and the authority-flow invariant.
Implement and test the invariant that authority only narrows downward.

Write the process-and-thread-model ADR including the explicit rejection of a Tokio replacement.

Implement the trap taxonomy: `QQQ-3001` memory, `QQQ-3002` fuel, `QQQ-3003` epoch.

Implement the invariant that guest-visible blocking host functions bypass host cooperative budgets.
Implement deterministic-mode engine configuration (NaN canonicalization, seeded RNG, fixed clock).
Implement instance metrics: acquire latency histogram, pool occupancy, trap counts by code.
Write the Wasmtime upgrade runbook and the compatibility-test suite.
Implement the module-preloading strategy for scale-out (compile on deploy, not on first request).
Implement resource-handle table pooling and lifetime diagnostics.
Implement `ResourcesRequired`-based admission control: refuse to load a component whose declared minimums exceed the host's capacity.
Port the three verification-probe assertions (missing-import failure, instantiation cost, fuel trap) into the permanent test suite and delete the scratch crate.
Implement the dual-ABI host: retain the 0.2 linker path and add a 0.3 path, with unknown imports failing closed on both, and instantiate a 0.2 guest and a 0.3 guest in the same build.
Measure WASI 0.3.1-feature support (`implements`, `map`) in the pinned wasmtime engine with a dedicated red-first test; record the blocker and stop the 0.3 path if unsupported.
Decide retire-or-keep for the 0.2 linker path with a recorded migration window, after determinism work settles.
Finalize and publish the `qqq.toml` JSON Schema.
Implement manifest parsing with schema-validated diagnostics naming the exact line.
Implement `qqq.toml` normalization: host patterns, secret references, path canonicalization.
Finalize and publish the `qqq.lock` schema including per-package `caps`.
Implement `lockfile-hash` covering all resolved artifacts and config.
Implement reproducible-build verification that fails when output digests are unstable.
Define the interface-versioning policy: SemVer per WIT package, `@since` mandatory.
Implement the CI check that every published WIT function carries `@since`.
Define and enforce the typed-error rule: every fallible host call returns `result<T, E>`.
Implement the CI check that no host interface reads an environment variable or the working directory implicitly.
Write the WIT style guide and enforce it in review.
Enforce the batch-first rule: implement a lint that flags list-shaped operations accepting single elements.
Implement the capability-name registry with a published, versioned list.
Implement `qqqai inspect`'s static capability analysis from the import table.
Define the deprecation mechanics in WIT: `@deprecated` with a removal version.
Implement the schema-drift CI check for the manifest, lockfile, CLI output and error catalogue.
Publish the contract-stability promise for each surface (WIT, manifest, lockfile, CLI JSON).
Implement the "no hidden global state" architecture test across all host interfaces.
Extend conformance execution to a 0.3 guest: fixtures, runner, and a dual-ABI instantiation case that fails closed on unknown imports.

Admit the WASI 0.2 baseline in `qqqai run` pre-flight without a grant: a normal `wasm32-wasip2` guest runs with an empty grant set; `qqq:` imports still require grants, unserved names still fail closed by name. Owns the `§O-782` pre-flight discovery.

Bind `qqq:secrets/secret-use` in the per-instance linker with the existing `host_secrets` module: `env:`-reference material resolution in the deploy layer, grant-gated operations, and `verify` record splitting; granted runs, ungranted fails at instantiation, unavailable and wrong-operation fail closed by WIT name. Owns the `§O-782`-class pre-flight gap for secrets (unmapped import refused by name).

Bind `qqq:env/environment` in the per-instance linker: manifest-allowlist reads only, no inherit; `not-allowed` (ungranted or unlisted) vs `unset` vs `invalid-utf8` distinguished by name; `allowed-names` lists the manifest set.

Bind `qqq:log/logging` in the per-instance linker: host-attributed tenant/trace identity, secret redaction outside guest reach, per-record size bound; `emit`, `emit-many`, and `enabled` against the operator log sink.

Bind `qqq:trace/tracing` in the per-instance linker: host-owned spans with enforced parentage, bounded attributes, W3C traceparent propagation; sampling decided by the host; spans exported through the operator channel (OTLP export stays OBS-012).

Bind `qqq:kv/store` in the per-instance linker: namespaced in-memory stores with TTL expiry, per-entry and quota bounds, sorted `keys`; read-only grants refuse writes by name; `stores` lists the manifest set.

Bind `qqq:queue/messaging` in the per-instance linker: bounded in-memory publish/subscribe with acknowledgement, lease expiry with redelivery, order-preserving `resolve-many` semantics; directions granted separately.

Bind `qqq:fs/filesystem` in the per-instance linker: preopened directory handles (no ambient paths), relative-name traversal refusal, mode enforcement (read-only/append-only/read-write), quotas, sorted entries; symlinks never escape the preopen.
Bind `qqq:dns/resolver` in the per-instance linker: manifest-allowlist resolution only, order-preserving `resolve-many`, bounded batch; `name-not-allowed` distinct from `not-found`.

Bind `qqq:sql/database` and `qqq:sql/transaction` in the per-instance linker against a process-local SQLite backend: typed prepare/query/execute with argument checks, row caps, read-only enforcement, commit-or-rollback transactions; non-`sqlite` drivers refuse as unusable databases by name.

Bind `qqq:crypto/hmac`, `qqq:crypto/aead`, and `qqq:crypto/signing` in the per-instance linker: allowlisted algorithms/constructions only, grant-gated operations, constant-time verify, typed WIT-error mapping; ungranted imports fail at instantiation, unlisted algorithms fail closed by name.
Implement the three capability kinds (resource, operation, ambient) as distinct types.
Implement step 1: PARSE, with schema validation and line-accurate diagnostics.
Implement step 2: NORMALIZE, including host-pattern expansion and secret-reference resolution.
Implement step 3: the developer-mode overlay, loudly non-production.
Implement step 4: the organization policy overlay, narrowing-only.
Implement step 5: the platform overlay, narrowing-only.
Implement step 6: RESOLVE to a serializable, hashable `Grants` set.
Implement step 7: BIND, constructing a per-instance linker from grants only.
Implement step 8: RECORD, hashing resolved grants into the audit record.
Prove the narrowing invariant with a test: no overlay configuration can widen a declared grant.
Implement the restricted policy expression language with static analysability and termination proofs.
Implement `qqqai why <resource>` producing the complete resolution chain.
Implement the ordered-map requirement: no host interface exposes unordered iteration to guests.
Implement per-tenant grant isolation and prove no cross-tenant handle leakage.
Implement capability-use accounting feeding the audit stream.
Implement the `qqq:secrets` interface: use a secret without disclosing it.
Model `[capabilities.sql]` in the manifest: typed struct, validation, grant derivation for `sql.query`/`sql.execute`, and a generator stanza that parses.
Model `[capabilities.kv]` in the manifest: typed struct, validation, grant derivation for `kv.read`/`kv.write`, and a generator stanza that parses.
Model `[capabilities.queue]` in the manifest: typed struct, validation, grant derivation for `queue.publish`/`queue.subscribe`, and a generator stanza that parses.
Model `[capabilities.ai]` in the manifest: typed struct, validation, grant derivation for `ai.infer`, and a generator stanza that parses.
Model `[capabilities.log]` in the manifest, preserving its ambient grant: typed struct, validation, and a generator stanza that parses.
Model `[capabilities.trace]` in the manifest, preserving its ambient grant: typed struct, validation, and a generator stanza that parses.
Model `[capabilities.secret]` in the manifest alongside the nested `crypto.secrets` spelling: typed struct, validation, grant derivation for `secret.use`, and a generator stanza that parses.

Derive `FsWatch` grants from `[[capabilities.fs]]` entries: decide which modes imply watch, wire it into `declared_capabilities`, and pin the `fs` stanza to grant it. The stanza today grants read/write only, so a watch denial pasted from `qqqai why` changes authority without granting watch.
Write the threat model document covering §7.1 assets and §7.2 adversaries.
Implement the rule that an ungranted import is absent, not merely denied, and prove it by test.
Implement manifest capability validation with a deny-by-default posture throughout.
Build the hostile-guest test suite (≥200 cases) with a specified expected failure for each.
Implement memory-limit enforcement and prove the host survives a guest OOM.
Implement fuel-limit enforcement and prove the host survives fuel exhaustion.
Implement epoch-deadline enforcement and prove the host survives a non-terminating guest.
Implement handle-count limits and prove the host survives handle exhaustion attempts.
Implement subrequest limits to prevent guest-driven request amplification.
Implement path-traversal defences at the capability boundary, with a test corpus.
Implement input validation at every guest-to-host boundary crossing.
Establish the fuzzing programme covering the host interfaces, manifest parser and component loader.
Add `cargo-fuzz` targets to CI with a nightly fuzzing schedule.
Establish the Wasmtime advisory-tracking process with a 72-hour patch target (`R-04`).
Implement the per-dependency capability diff display at install time.
Implement slow-loris, header-bomb and body-bomb mitigations with tests.
Implement the cryptographic-posture policy: named algorithms, no silent defaults, no agility without a version bump.
Implement the host CSPRNG with no guest-supplied seed outside deterministic test mode.
Implement Linux hardening: dropped privileges, `no_new_privs`, seccomp allowlist.
Audit every `unsafe` block in the three exception crates and record the findings.
Track post-quantum hybrid TLS (X25519+ML-KEM) as an opt-in, with a standards-watch task.
Implement the optional egress proxy with per-tenant policy.
Establish the responsible-disclosure process and a public security-advisory feed.

Commission external security audit #2 before the public beta (M10).
Implement Landlock LSM integration as defence in depth on Linux ≥ 5.13.

Implement memory-protection-key support as an optional hardening feature. Owner: Systems engineer. Detection done (below); enforcement blocked on (1) `qqq-sys` admitting `unsafe` via the SAFETY.md exception process (needs second maintainer, GOV-008), (2) MPK crates that are not thin `unsafe` FFI wrappers, (3) pku-capable hardware to exercise it on.
Produce and publish the SBOM for every release.
Implement the distroless, read-only, non-root container image.
Publish the explicit out-of-scope section (host admin, side channels, physical, volumetric DoS).
Implement HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive, timeouts and connection limits.
Implement HTTP/2 including multiplexing and flow control.
Implement the compile-time route table as a radix trie.
Implement streaming bodies end to end with backpressure propagation.

Implement mTLS as a supported `default_auth` mode.
Implement WebSockets over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.
Implement Server-Sent Events.
Implement graceful shutdown with in-flight request draining.
Implement per-tenant connection limits and idle timeouts.
Implement structured access logging with tenant and trace correlation.

Implement CORS configuration with safe defaults.

Record the `abi.host` policy decision: WASI releases never bump `abi.host`; only an incompatible QQQ-interface change does (with the comparison that justifies no-bump, or the bump with its host-gated rollout).
Implement `qqqai new` scaffolding for all five languages and five templates.

Implement the "your app has 0 capabilities" guidance shown at dev-server start.
Implement the error-message standard: what, code, why, fix, machine block.

Blocked on review plus merge gates: versioned generation leases, live HTTP dispatch and dev rebuild activation are implemented in the live-components draft; `docs/live-components-checklist.md` names the measured acceptance, failure controls and remaining merge gates. Implement TIER-2 state-preserving swap with declared guest state. Owner: Architect. Blocked behind the TIER-1 review and a state-declaration design: guest state shape, migration, and failure semantics are undecided.

Implement TIER-3 full restart triggered only by manifest capability or limit changes. Owner: Architect. Blocked behind the TIER-1 review: trigger conditions and restart atomicity ride on the same merge decision.
Implement the file watcher with debounce and ignore rules.

Implement HTTPS in dev with locally-trusted certificates. Owner: Architect. Blocked on a trust decision: minting locally-trusted certificates means installing a CA into the developer's trust store, and doing that silently would be a security posture set by tooling rather than by the operator.

Implement `qqqai trace`. Owner: Architect. Blocked on the trace-consumption design: the command falls through to "not implemented yet", and what `trace` shows (live spans? recorded audits? which tenant's?) is undecided — building a surface before its contract is how `doctor` needed four defect fixes after landing.
Implement `qqqai doctor`.

Implement the POSIX `install.sh` installer with checksum and signature verification. Owner: Release engineer. Blocked on the release pipeline: `tools/bootstrap.sh` onboards developers, but a user-facing installer needs signed artifacts to verify plus the checksum/signature publication flow, none of which exist yet.
Implement the Windows `install.ps1` installer with the same verification. Owner: Release engineer. Blocked on the same release pipeline as DIST-001, plus Windows code signing (see DIST-016).
